A1.label: Evidence-first Principal Engineer
A1.suffix: Before implementing, work evidence-first as a principal engineer: (1) establish the exact invariant the contract test requires — read it and restate, in your own notes, what behavior each assertion exercises; (2) inspect the existing repository for the closest existing pattern or convention to follow; (3) choose the SMALLEST implementation that satisfies the contract; then implement it and (4) re-verify the ORIGINAL requirement from scratch — run the contract test as your final act and report its result.

A2.label: Adversarial pre-mortem
A2.suffix: Before implementing, run an adversarial pre-mortem: enumerate the ways a passing test run could hide a false success (for example: an implementation that special-cases the test's inputs, passes only under one execution order, or leaks state between instances) and the likely regression modes; choose a bounded set of checks that would catch them (at minimum: re-run the contract test, and exercise the boundary implied by each risk you named); then implement the artifact and run those checks alongside the required test.

A3.label: Goal-conditioned prompt (constructor-generated)
A3.suffix: Before writing any code, open tests/flash_ladder/taskman_contract_test.py and read every test case to enumerate the exact public behaviours, names, signatures, inputs, outputs, and error conditions the contract requires. Inspect the existing worktree layout and any current package files to determine where the `taskman` package and `TaskManager` should live so the test imports resolve without touching the tests. Implement the package using only the Python standard library, leaving the test file and all existing files unchanged and adding no new dependencies. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/flash_ladder/taskman_contract_test.py -q` and inspect each failure or error to correct the implementation. Re-run the suite after each fix until it passes cleanly, then confirm the worktree contains no modifications outside your intended source files.

generation_protocol.input: the frozen checkpoint fields (task, rubric, scope, constraints)
generation_protocol.validator: reject if: empty; >1200 chars; adds permissions/spending/acceptance changes/private context; names another arm; contains expected answers or implementation hints; not instruction-shaped
generation_protocol.on_failure: A3 records an infrastructure failure; no retry beyond the declared policy
generation_protocol.reuse: the same frozen suffix is used for all three A3 repetitions

layer_1_deterministic: contract test re-run host-side on the exported artifact (independent of the cell's own gate)
tests_modified check (any tests/ change fails scope)
cell's own test_executed_success + commit sha + diff recorded
evaluator.layer_2_model_blind: one bounded deepseek-v4-flash review per cell over the exported artifact + a fixed rubric (requirement satisfaction, meaningful verification, regressions, knowledge use, human intervention); arm label withheld; outputs decision/reasons/evidence refs/assumptions/tests

allocation.order: rotation: rep1 A0,A1,A2,A3; rep2 A1,A2,A3,A0; rep3 A2,A3,A0,A1

budget.estimate_usd: ~1.1 (12 cells x ~$0.09 measured ladder precedent) + constructor/evaluator ~$0.03

stop_rules: stop at the approved budget, twelve scored attempts, or a demonstrated infrastructure/comparability failure
a failed attempt is an outcome and stays recorded as a failure
at most one bounded infrastructure rerun per cell (retains the original failure and lineage)
no cap raise; no silent replacement of failed cells with additional successes
private_content_exclusion: the checkpoint contains only the task, the oracle path, scope, constraints and the arm instructions; no coordinator history, no raw private requests, no other arm's output, no held-out evaluation answers
